Earlier neural concepts are treated as learned only at the explicit prior chapter passages cited in relation evidence and the Stage3 prerequisite map. No seed knowledge is assumed: the premature term was removed at p66. Undergraduate calculus, basic probability and linear algebra, with expected value, variance, SD and density known. The new Part also uses actual earlier teaching: Poisson/CV (foundations and eye circuit), covariance/shared sources (eye drift), Brownian filtering (eye timing), Euler (preceding memory simulation), fields/grid/topology (place chapters), and hardware evidence types (PartIII). These are earlier-reading prerequisites, not unstated innate background. Undergraduate calculus, linear algebra and basic probability, with expectation/variance/SD/density known. At ch20 entry, the earlier place-field sequence has taught Gaussian fields, covariance, thresholds, scale, likelihood comparisons, high-threshold laws, Betti/EC and median filtering; these specific prior teachings were checked, not inferred from expertise.
